title: Redwood + VentraCloud marketplace integration tech sync
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-07-28
Start: 09:23 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Yes
Attendees: Evan, Priya, Matt (Redwood); Aisha, Jon, Eric, Lina (VentraCloud)
summary: Technical sync to finalize Marketplace listing checklist, discuss reference architecture for private VPC deployment, and align on joint solution collateral and security requirements. Key asks: security docs (SOC2/ISO evidence), reference arch diagram for VentraCloud marketplace onboarding, test tenant for end-to-end listing, and timeline for public listing (target late Aug).
topics: Marketplace listing requirements and gap list
Reference architecture for Redwood Private on VentraCloud (VPC + KMS integration)
Joint solution listing/marketing collateral and reference arch diagram
Integration checklist: SSO/SAML, API keys, billing metadata
transcript:
00:00 Evan Brooks: okay good morning everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes. um quick intros?
00:08 Aisha Rahman: hi i'm aisha, head of cloud partnerships at ventracloud, thanks for setting this up.
00:12 Jon Park: jon here, product manager for marketplace listings.
00:15 Priya Nair: priya, systems eng on redwood, focus on private deployments and integrations.
00:18 Eric Muller: eric, security at ventra, i'll be handling the compliance questions.
00:22 Matt Gomez: matt, solutions architect, i'll run through the reference arch.
00:25 Lina Torres: lina, devops — i'll be the technical owner for the infra side.
00:30 Evan Brooks: awesome. quick agenda — marketplace checklist, then reference architecture deep dive, security & intake, and then action items. sound good?
00:37 Aisha Rahman: yep good.
00:40 Jon Park: yep.
00:42 Matt Gomez: starting with marketplace — we've been through the standard ventra checklist, right? images, pricing metadata, deployment options. Evan, can you summarize redwood's supported listing modes?
00:55 Evan Brooks: sure — we support hosted api (redwood hosted), dedicated/reserved capacity for enterprise customers, and private deployments (vpc/on-prem). for marketplace listing we typically list two SKUs — hosted api quickstart and managed private (bring-your-own infra or ventra managed). important note: names sometimes get munged in the marketplace UI so we recommend "Redwood Inference — Hosted API" and "Redwood Inference — Private (VentraCloud Reference)".
01:20 Jon Park: ok, naming is fine. inventory question: for the private listing, do you provide an AMI / image or a reference architecture only?
01:28 Priya Nair: good question — our private offering is a reference arch + deployment automation (terraform + helm charts) — we can provide a marketplace image if the partner requires it but typically we do a marketplace listing that links to a deployment doc and a partner-provisioned listing. in ventra's case we can provide a reference arch that integrates with ventra's KMS and marketplace provisioning hooks.
01:46 Lina Torres: that works. we prefer a deployment module (terraform) so partners can automate tenant creation. how does redwood manage secrets / keys for private installs?
01:55 Matt Gomez: we support external KMS (customer-managed) — we have a KMS integration layer in the control plane; keys never leave the customer's KMS. for marketplace we can call out an optional ventra-kms integration step in the doc.
02:10 Eric Muller: from sec perspective we need evidence — SOC 2 or ISO attestations, data flows, audit log retention, and an architectural diagram that shows the control plane boundaries. do you have a versioned reference arch we can consume?
02:22 Priya Nair: yes — we'll share a versioned reference arch diagram. note: our control plane in the private model is an optional customer-managed control plane or a lightweight redwood control plane that can be run in ventra's VPC with restricted network egress. sometimes docs call it 'Redwood Private Control Panel' — sorry that product naming is inconsistent in older docs.
02:42 Aisha Rahman: haha, yeah we've seen 'control plane' and 'admin plane' used interchangeably — okay send the canonical diagram.
02:49 Evan Brooks: we'll upload the diagram to the shared drive and link it in the marketplace listing.
02:53 Jon Park: good. on billing/integration, ventra's marketplace requires metadata for meter dimensions and a webhook for provisioning status. can redwood push provisioning events back to our hooks?
03:05 Priya Nair: yes we've implemented provisioning callbacks for other partners. we can emit a standard lifecycle webhook and include provisioning state and tenant id. format will be JSON; we'll share the webhook schema.
03:15 Lina Torres: what's the auth model for the webhook? we need HMAC signing.
03:18 Matt Gomez: we can sign payloads with an HMAC using a shared secret; we also support mutual TLS if ventra prefers.
03:26 Eric Muller: perfect. on encryption at rest — are model weights encrypted? what about KV cache?
03:31 Priya Nair: weights inside our runtime are consumed decrypted by the runtime when loaded but can be stored encrypted at rest using the customer's KMS. KV cache and token caches are encrypted at rest as well. there's an optional in-memory-only mode for KV cache for customers with strict requirements.
03:47 Evan Brooks: small note — sometimes on calls we call it 'KV cache' and other docs use 'key-value cache' or 'kv-cache' — just flagging possible doc mismatch in marketplace copy.
03:55 Jon Park: ha, noted. ok reference arch — matt, you had a slide?
04:00 Matt Gomez: yes, let me talk through the recommended topology: ventra-managed VPC with private subnets for inference workers, a dedicated NAT for outbound updates only, control plane either run as customer-managed in the same VPC or run in redwood's mgmt plane with strict network peering. we recommend three components: model serving pool, control plane, and observability stack. observability hooks send traces and token-level cost metrics to redwood console — in private we can route metrics to ventra's prometheus/loki if you want.
04:27 Lina Torres: prometheus is preferred. we need all telemetry to stay inside our environment unless an explicit opt-in is configured.
04:33 Priya Nair: that's supported — we ship a metrics exporter and a prom remote_write config. we'll document the steps.
04:40 Eric Muller: audit logs — retention policy? can we configure TTL?
04:44 Matt Gomez: yes logs retention is configurable; for private installs it's controlled by a config in the operator. defaults are 90 days but can be extended. we'll document storage sizing guidance.
04:55 Aisha Rahman: timeline question — jon asked for public listing by late august. is that feasible?
04:59 Evan Brooks: with a target we can do it — contingency: we'll need the security pack and test tenant by 2027-08-12 to validate everything end-to-end.
05:09 Jon Park: that's doable on our side if we get docs this week.
05:12 Priya Nair: action: we'll share the security pack (SOC2 report redacted) and the canonical reference arch by 2027-07-30. can ventra commit to provisioning a test tenant by 2027-08-05?
05:22 Aisha Rahman: yes we'll try for the 5th. Lina will own it.
05:26 Lina Torres: yep i'll create a test project and provide creds.
05:29 Evan Brooks: great. let's walk the checklist quickly — item one: marketplace listing metadata (we'll supply marketplace copy / images) — jon will review.
05:40 Jon Park: i'll share the marketplace content template after the call.
05:44 Priya Nair: item two: security/compliance pack — redwood to send SOC2 summary and control mappings.
05:50 Matt Gomez: item three: reference arch + terraform module — we'll share repo with example tf module and helm values.
05:57 Eric Muller: will the module include hardening defaults?
06:00 Priya Nair: yes, defaults include restricted security groups, pod security standards, and KMS integration steps.
06:06 Aisha Rahman: i have a question about support model post-listing — if a customer buys the ventra marketplace private listing, who handles first-level support?
06:14 Evan Brooks: typically ventra handles infra-level L1 and we handle product-level L2 — we can formalize an escalation matrix. we'll include a short runbook for common incidents.
06:24 Jon Park: ok. any competitors we should call out in copy?
06:27 Aisha Rahman: we generally avoid naming competitors directly on the marketplace page but we do provide comparison docs. who did you say are the main competitors?
06:34 Evan Brooks: from our POV it's a mix: big cloud vendors' managed LLM endpoints and specialized inference vendors — we can provide a neutral "compare" doc.
06:42 Priya Nair: i'll add a short one-page comparison we can include in the partner portal.
06:46 Jon Park: operational question — load testing and performance benchmarks, will ventra allow us to run baseline throughput tests in the test tenant?
06:54 Lina Torres: yes but within quotas — we'll coordinate a schedule and expected test harness.
06:58 Matt Gomez: superfine. we'll provide a benchmark harness (locust-based) and suggested instance types.
07:05 Eric Muller: final sec Q: do you do VPC peering or PrivateLink style connectivity?
07:10 Priya Nair: we support both; PrivateLink is recommended for full network isolation, but peerings work for some setups — we'll document both options and recommended firewall rules.
07:20 Evan Brooks: ok wrapping — recap of next steps: redwood to send security pack and canonical reference arch by 2027-07-30; redwood to share terraform module and helm charts; ventra to provision test tenant by 2027-08-05; schedule end-to-end validation week of 2027-08-09; target public listing late August.
07:40 Aisha Rahman: sounds good.
07:43 Jon Park: i'll send the marketplace template today.
07:46 Evan Brooks: action items we'll capture and email, also we'll drop the reference diagrams in the shared drive. thanks everyone.
07:53 Speaker 6: thanks.
07:55 Evan Brooks: bye all.
08:00 END OF RECORDING

Notes: transcription has modest ASR errors — some proper nouns and product names may be inconsistent (e.g., Redwood Private / control panel naming). The team used shorthand (KV cache, prom). There was occasional crosstalk and quick interruptions.
